narrative.overview:
Signal is a cool-paper engineering editorial: precise graphite geometry, violet emphasis, generous breathing room, and code with a real job to do. The owner-approved world is confident without becoming a dashboard or a decorative card collection. The sharp violet woodpecker/f with a coral beak and crest carries the identity; the drifting dot field remains the signature atmospheric material.

The visual language stays shared while density follows the task. Persuade surfaces give the headline and working code room to lead. Read surfaces quiet the decoration and prioritize navigation, line length, and document hierarchy. Operate surfaces spend their width on source, diagnostics, output, and generated JavaScript. These are different applications of the same system, not a requirement to reuse the homepage composition everywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper, graphite text, and restrained violet signals.
Geist editorial hierarchy paired with practical monospace code.
Unboxed content sections, fine rules, and small controlled radii.
Real interactive examples with explicit loading, failure, and recovery states.
A static dot geometry with one slow group drift honoring system reduced motion.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet denotes identity, action, selection, focus, or language structure; neutral ink carries ordinary reading.

rules.name: The Code Is Content Rule
rules.body: Preserve code whitespace, line breaks, and horizontal access to long lines; never shrink the whole page to fit a source line.

rules.name: The Task-Width Rule
rules.body: Keep reading columns bounded, but give Play and Transpile their wider workspace; the document measure is not the editor measure.

dos: **Do** reuse semantic theme properties so controls, code, and reading surfaces respond together to theme changes.
**Do** keep reading measures bounded and allow Play and Transpile the wider workspace.
**Do** preserve the approved woodpecker/f silhouette, angular eye, three-tip horizontal wing, coral accents and shallow relief; keep the fine rules and restrained corners.
**Do** keep source whitespace, keyboard focus, localized labels, and explicit recovery feedback intact.
**Do** author custom widget state and behavior in Flick, leaving platform interoperability and mounting at the JavaScript/TypeScript boundary.
**Do** honor system reduced-motion preferences; animate the wave as one group only.
donts: **Don't** turn every feature or destination into an elevated card; the shipped editorial sections and ruled rows are intentionally open.
**Don't** copy the homepage's headline/editor composition into every reading or operating surface.
**Don't** remove mobile access to locales, reference navigation, or Transpile when compacting the header.
**Don't** replace real compiler output, copy failures, diagnostics, or loading states with ornamental success claims.
**Don't** add per-dot animation or atmospheric motion to reading and editing surfaces.
